title: Memory of the past
html_source:
The opera Maritana by William Vincent Wallace contains a song “There is a Flower That Bloometh.” The title could not be more pertinent, either for the novel Ulysses or for the goings on at this point in Circe. The card Bloom has been carrying in his hat since morning, the card bearing the name “Henry Flower” he used as ID to get his letter from Martha Clifford that morning from the post office. This is the “Flower” that “Bloometh.” Now, as defendant in his “trial,” he appears, “holding a fullblown waterlily,” symbol of purity of heart. In the opera, Don Caesar has been tricked into marrying Maritana, and is unhappy, not knowing who she was, veiled as she had been for the ceremony. Maritana is now gone from his life, and he sings, “There is a flower that bloometh / When autumn leaves are shed. /… Oh, pluck it ere it wither, / ‘Tis the memory of the past// It wafted perfume o'er us, / Of sweet, though sad regret / For the true friends gone before us, / Whom none would e’re forget. / Let no heart brave its power, / By guilty thoughts o'ercast, / For then, a poison flow'r / Is – the memory of the past.”

If Bloom ever had true friends, there are none there to defend him. He was washed over in loneliness and the poison flower of guilty thoughts of his bad behavior, the memories of the past.

There is linkage between the Don Caesar/ Maritana couple and the Blooms. Leopold has not known who Molly is (nor, certainly, she him) and he has believed she is now is gone, at least, emotionally, from him forever. “All is lost,” the title to another aria from the opera Martha with deep significance to Ulysses.
